In plain words

The article tested 25 popular tools that developers use to download third-party code and found that many would accept altered code if the service providing it were compromised. This can affect software developers and the users of applications built with these tools, because harmful code could be quietly added to otherwise legitimate software components. The article argues that these tools should check downloaded code against trusted records or digital proof of who created it, so a compromised download service cannot secretly change what people install.

Summary
Testing of 25 popular package managers found that fewer than half enforce lockfile hash integrity by default, and only Go verifies every downloaded package and signatures by default against a compromised repository. Stronger supply-chain protection requires default hash/signature verification, trusted identity-based signing, and transparency logs rather than relying on repositories or lockfiles that can be silently updated.

Trail of Bits tested 25 popular source-code package managers by simulating a compromised package repository that inserted malicious code into legitimate downloaded packages. Fewer than half of the tested managers used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only Go and vcpkg verified package integrity in the tested default configurations. The tests found that many tools either lacked integrity checks, required extra configuration, or used lockfile data in ways that did not block altered packages. cpanminus was a notable exception to widespread HTTPS use because it connected to the Perl repository over unencrypted HTTP by default.

The article explains that hashes in lockfiles can protect downloads only when the package manager securely verifies them and refuses mismatches. For example, Pub detected a changed package hash but installed the package and updated its lockfile by default, while pnpm had similar behavior until version 11.4. Package signatures and Sigstore-based attestations are available in several ecosystems, but many clients do not validate them by default or require separate commands and manual trusted-key configuration. Go performed best in the tests by checking downloaded package hashes against a signed checksum database, though this design concentrates trust in the database signing key.

  • A lockfile can contain a cryptographic hash without providing protection: Pub detects a hash mismatch by default but still installs the package and rewrites the lockfile unless the user enables --enforce-lockfile.
  • pnpm also updated lockfiles after a mismatch by default until version 11.4 in May 2026, showing that lockfile behavior intended for dependency updates can undermine tamper detection.
  • The existence of package signatures does not ensure protection, because npm requires a separate npm audit signatures command and NuGet's default mode accepts packages with invalid signatures.
  • Developer signing can protect packages from a compromised repository, but systems that require developers to manage long-lived keys risk preventing future updates if the developer loses the key.
  • Go's checksum database provides strong default integrity checks, but its registry-signature-style model concentrates substantial trust in the private key used to sign that database.
Key Points
  • 01The author tested 25 popular source-code package managers against a simulated compromised package repository that injected malicious code into legitimate packages.
  • 02Fewer than half of the tested package managers used lockfiles that detect tampering by default, and only Go and vcpkg verified package integrity in the tested default configurations.
  • 03Many package managers can store hashes in lockfiles, but some either update the lockfile after detecting a mismatch or use hashes that do not verify the downloaded package contents.
  • 04Although package signatures and provenance attestations exist in several ecosystems, many clients do not verify them by default or require users to configure trusted signing keys manually.
  • 05Go was the only tested package manager that verified signatures by default, using a signed checksum database and a transparency-log-style design to compare package contents.

IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report finds that AI-driven and shadow-AI incidents are rising sharply, largely because organizations lack effective access controls and governance around AI systems and their data connections. IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report, based on 602 organizations and 3,558 security and C-suite leaders, found that the global average cost of a data breach reached \(4.99 million, up 12% from the prior year. AI-driven attacks rose 56%, with more than one in four organizations that experienced a malicious attack saying AI was involved. Deepfake impersonation and AI-generated malware accounted for much of this increase and added an average of \)1 million per breach.

The report found that AI-related breaches were usually caused by weaknesses around AI systems, including compromised APIs, connected applications, cloud misconfigurations, and inadequate access controls. Ninety-two percent of AI-related breaches involved no proper AI access controls, while shadow AI incidents more than doubled to 43% and nearly half resulted in data loss or compromise. Organizations that used AI and automation extensively throughout prevention, detection, investigation, and response reduced breach costs by $1.93 million and shortened breach timelines by 65 days compared with organizations that did not.

  • The report indicates that the most costly AI incidents usually stem from the systems connected to an AI model, such as APIs, applications, and cloud settings, rather than from flaws in the model itself.
  • Model inversion and prompt injection were the most expensive reported AI attack types, averaging $6.07 million and $5.89 million respectively, because recovery can require governance and disclosure work beyond technical remediation.
  • AI governance was absent at 68% of breached organizations, but only 19% of organizations reported coordination between their governance and security teams, highlighting an operational disconnect rather than simply a missing policy.
  • Although half of breached organizations had deployed AI agents in their security operations centers, only 18% used them for vulnerability scanning and management, while most use was concentrated in detection and investigation.
  • Financial services and energy accounted for 62% of the AI-driven breaches studied despite identifying and containing breaches roughly four weeks faster than the global average.

  • 03Among organizations reporting an AI-related breach, 92% lacked proper AI access controls, while only 40% reported using access controls on AI models and data.

  • 05Organizations that used AI and automation extensively across their security lifecycle reduced average breach costs by $1.93 million and shortened breach timelines by 65 days.

Across nine metered Codex sessions, the release-candidate workstream recorded $815.50 in model spend, 1.29474 billion reported tokens, and 93 hours and 43 minutes of agent time; the maintainer still manually reviewed critical workflows, including MFA behavior and login transitions, before release acceptance.

  • The largest session accounted for about 59% of model spending because the initial design direction was ambiguous, illustrating that unclear goals can be more costly than large implementation work with concrete success criteria.
  • Higher-capability model use was not permanent: after Sol identified TinyMCE initialization inside inactive Bootstrap tabs as the cause of a flicker, the team made the architectural decision to standardize on Tiptap and routed the resulting migration back to Terra.
  • Repeated reviews by Terra across 161 templates continued finding missed pages rather than converging, so the team escalated to Sol for a broader final review that eventually found no additional missed templates.
  • The mixed-model workstream cost only $89.06 less than repricing the recorded token volume entirely at Sol’s medium-effort rate, because the project legitimately required substantial high-capability work for design exploration, diagnosis, and consequential review.
  • The team started new sessions when context approached roughly 75% of capacity or after a significant body of work was completed, treating session boundaries as a way to prevent stale discussion from influencing new tasks.
Key Points
  • 01SpecterOps advocates an AI Engagement Model in which people frame a problem, challenge assumptions, verify results, decide on a direction, and then ask an AI agent to produce implementation work.
  • 02For Ghostwriter’s interface refresh, SpecterOps used less expensive models for bounded questions and clear changes, while reserving more capable models for ambiguous design, difficult diagnosis, and broader review.
  • 03The Ghostwriter refresh updated 99 screens and 161 template files, upgraded the application to Bootstrap 5.3, and introduced an expandable dashboard, engagement bar, and customizable sidebar.
  • 04The nine metered Codex sessions associated with the Ghostwriter v7.3.0 release-candidate workstream recorded $815.50 in model spend, 1.29474 billion reported tokens, and 93 hours and 43 minutes of agent time.

Summary
Threat hunting is a continuous-improvement cycle, not merely a way to find active incidents: each investigation should strengthen detections, baselines, visibility, and future hunting hypotheses. Even hunts that find no threat provide valuable validation and identify gaps to fix.

Threat hunting is presented as a continuous improvement process rather than an effort focused solely on finding active security incidents. Its purpose is to reduce the likelihood of future harmful activity by improving an organization’s defenses, knowledge, and ability to recognize unusual behavior. Like debugging software, each investigation can reveal lessons that make future problems less likely. The process is cyclical, with each hunt feeding improvements into the next one.

Teams can focus hunts using informed hypotheses, maps of normal activity, statistical tools such as RITA, or machine-learning models that flag deviations from expected behavior. Investigations typically begin broadly, filter out known-good activity, and follow connections across accounts, logs, and source IP addresses while considering operational context. A hunt that finds no threat can still validate that defenses work or reveal absent and misconfigured detections. Findings should be converted into detection rules, documented baselines, shared knowledge, closed visibility gaps, and new hypotheses, with sustained programs potentially accelerating in value after 12–18 months.

  • A hunt that finds no active threat is still valuable because it can confirm defenses are working or expose detections that are missing or misconfigured.
  • The article emphasizes that an unusual event is not automatically harmful; its meaning depends on operational context, such as a database administrator running unusual queries during a production emergency.
  • The most durable outcome of a hunt is turning manual investigation knowledge into detection rules, so teams do not need to repeatedly hunt for the same behavior.
  • Sustained hunting programs can reach a point after roughly 12–18 months where accumulated knowledge makes their value increase dramatically.
Key Points
  • 01The goal of threat hunting is to continuously improve a security program and reduce the likelihood of future harmful activity, not simply to find current incidents.

AI systems concept

anthropic

artificial intelligence concept

nuget
NuGet is Microsoft’s package manager for .NET software libraries.
Numi AI product
Numi AI is an AI product referenced as coordinating specialized software agents.

Microsoft's monthly October 2026 release of software security updates.

The October 2026 Patch Tuesday update is a Microsoft software patch released in its regular monthly update cycle.

office
Microsoft Office is a productivity suite that includes apps like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

A one-time code is a short temporary code used to confirm identity during login or a transaction.

OneDrive is Microsoft's cloud storage service for saving and syncing files online.
also: tenant's SharePoint and OneDrive

A cybercrime-related Telegram group reportedly used to offer tools for carrying out scams.

Accounts used to access internet services such as email, cloud storage, social media, or websites.
online marketplace concept
An online marketplace is a website or platform where buyers and sellers exchange goods or services.
online persona concept
An identity or character someone presents online, often through accounts, usernames, posts, and other activity.

online scams concept
Internet-based frauds that trick people into giving away money, information, or account access.
online services concept
Online services are websites, apps, or internet-based systems that provide functions to users over the internet.
open source concept
Open source means software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, and share.

also: ChatGPT-maker
OpenAI Dot product
An OpenAI product or service referenced in security reporting.
OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol product
OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol is an AI model name referenced in reporting.
openid protocol
An OpenID Connect scope that requests basic identity information during sign-in.

Operation Lonestar Roundup other
A named law-enforcement operation targeting suspected criminal activity.

Operational inspections are surveillance activities used to collect information from a target or system.
Operational software concept
Software used to run, manage, or support an organization's activities.
Operational technology concept
Operational technology is hardware and software used to monitor or control physical equipment, such as factory machines, power systems, or industrial sensors.

An Operator is a Kubernetes automation component that manages an application by encoding operational tasks into software.
operators concept
Operators are the people or groups running a system, service, campaign, or criminal operation.
Opposition Leaders concept
Opposition leaders are political figures who challenge or are not part of the governing administration.
oracle
Oracle is a technology company known for databases, enterprise software, cloud services, and Java-related products.
Oracle Linux product
Oracle Linux is a Linux operating system distribution maintained by Oracle.
Oracle Linux product
Oracle Linux is Oracle’s Linux operating system distribution for servers and enterprise use.
Organizational context concept
Organizational context is background information about a company or agency that helps explain its risks, systems, and decisions.
Origin concept
The central security project where detection activity and investigation records are managed.
OT concept
OT, or operational technology, is hardware and software that monitors or controls physical equipment like factory machines or power systems.
OTP concept
A temporary authentication code valid for a single session or transaction, used to add extra security beyond passwords.

A technique where a compromised system makes a network connection back to the attacker on a separate channel to confirm exploitation or evade detection.

Out-of-band verification means confirming a request through a separate communication channel, such as calling a known phone number instead of replying to an email.
outage concept
A period when a service, website, or network is unavailable, often caused by cyberattacks like DDoS or system failures.
outbound connections concept
Outbound connections are network connections that start from inside a system or network and go out to another destination.

Outdated means software, data, or settings are old and may be missing important fixes or protections.

Outdated firmware is old device software that may be missing important security fixes.

Outflank is a cybersecurity company known for red-team and adversary-simulation tools and services.
oversight concept
Oversight means watching over an activity or organization to make sure rules are followed and problems are caught.

OWASP is a nonprofit security organization best known for publishing widely used guidance on web application risks.
OWASP Top 10 concept
OWASP Top 10 is a widely used list of the most important web application security risks.
PA-Series product
A line of physical next-generation firewall appliances made by Palo Alto Networks.
package manager tool
A package manager is software that installs, updates, and manages libraries or applications for developers and operating systems.
package managers tool
Package managers are tools that install, update, and manage software libraries or applications.
package update concept
A package update is a newer version of a software component that may include fixes, features, or security patches.
packet capture technique
Packet capture is the recording of network traffic so it can be inspected and analyzed.
also: packet-capture rules, sniffer configurations
Palo Alto organization
Palo Alto refers to Palo Alto Networks, a cybersecurity company known for firewalls and cloud security products.
Palo Alto Networks organization
A leading global cybersecurity company known for next-generation firewalls and advanced cloud security.
PAN-OS product
PAN-OS is the operating system that runs Palo Alto Networks firewalls and security appliances.
Panorama product
A Palo Alto Networks product for centrally managing firewall policies, settings, and devices.
also: Panorama virtual
Parsing technique
Breaking raw data into structured pieces so software or people can search and use it.
password guessing technique
Password guessing is trying likely passwords until one works.
Patch Status concept
Information showing whether a device has installed available software updates that fix known problems.
Patch Tuesday concept
Patch Tuesday is Microsoft's regular monthly release day for security updates, usually the second Tuesday of each month.
Patch Tuesday release concept
A Patch Tuesday release is Microsoft’s regular monthly bundle of security and software updates.
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patched version concept
A patched version is a software release that includes fixes for bugs or security vulnerabilities.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.

payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
payloads concept
Payloads are the parts of malware or an exploit that perform the attacker's intended action, such as stealing data or installing ransomware.
payment card product
A payment card is a credit, debit, or similar card used to pay for goods and services.

Payment fraud is the unauthorized or deceptive use of payment methods to steal money or goods.
payment information concept
Payment information is data used to make purchases, such as card numbers, billing details, or payment account identifiers.

Records and processes used by an organization to pay its workers.
PDF reports concept
Documents in Portable Document Format, commonly used to share reports in a fixed layout.

also: PEERSTITCH implant, PEERSTITCH malware

Pegasus is a powerful commercial spyware tool known for infecting phones to secretly monitor messages, calls, location, and other data.

Pegasus spyware is NSO Group’s commercial surveillance malware that can secretly infect smartphones and collect messages, calls, location, and other private data.
penetration testing framework tool
A collection of tools and features used by authorized testers to find and demonstrate security weaknesses.
pentest technique
A pentest, short for penetration test, is an authorized attempt to find and exploit security weaknesses.

Pentesting is authorized hacking performed to find and help fix security weaknesses.
Perl product
Perl is a programming language commonly used for scripting and text processing.
persist() technique
A Spark operation that keeps data in memory or storage so it can be reused more quickly.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
persistent malware malware
Persistent malware is malicious software designed to stay on a device and keep running even after reboots or attempted cleanup.
personal data concept
Information relating to an identifiable individual, such as name, email, location, or financial details.
personal details concept
Personal details are information about a person, such as their name, address, phone number, or financial data, that can be misused if stolen.
personal information concept
Personal information is data that can identify or describe a person, such as a name, address, phone number, or account details.
personally identifiable information concept
Personally identifiable information is data that can identify a person, such as a name, address, Social Security number, or email address.
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) concept
Information that can identify a particular person, such as their name, address, or account details.
also: financial PII
philippines other
The Philippines is a country in Southeast Asia that may be mentioned in cyber reports as a victim location, actor location, or operating base.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.

A phishing email is a fake or deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or clicking something harmful.
phishing emails technique

also: phishing emails and SMS messages, phishing messages, phishing lure

also: phishing kit
phishing-as-a-service concept

also: PhaaS, PaaS

phone numbers concept
Phone numbers are the unique numbers used to reach people or devices on telephone networks.
PHP protocol
PHP is a programming language commonly used to build websites.
also: PHP files

A PHP file is a web server script file written in the PHP programming language.

PHP web shells are small scripts attackers place on a web server so they can run commands through a browser.
Physical Access concept
The ability to enter or directly handle a building, device, or other physical asset.
Picus organization
A cybersecurity company that provides automated breach and attack simulation to help organizations test their defenses continuously.
Picus Exposure Validation product
Picus Exposure Validation is a Picus Security product for testing whether security weaknesses can be used in realistic attack paths.
Picus Swarm product
Picus Swarm is a cybersecurity product or platform referenced in security reporting.
picus-security organization
Picus Security is a cybersecurity company known for attack simulation and validation tools.
pig-butchering technique
Pig-butchering is a long-running scam where criminals build trust with a victim before tricking them into fake investments.
PII concept
PII means personally identifiable information, such as names, addresses, ID numbers, or other data that can identify a person.
PINs concept
PINs are short secret number codes used to verify identity or authorize access.
pip tool
pip is the standard package installer used to download and install Python software libraries.
planner tool
A component that breaks a larger task into smaller jobs for other automated agents to perform.

Playwright is a tool developers and testers use to automate web browsers like Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.
pnpm tool
pnpm is a fast JavaScript package manager used to install and manage project dependencies.
Podcast concept
A podcast is an online audio or video show that people can stream or download, sometimes used to share security news or analysis.
point-in-time assessment concept
A point-in-time assessment checks security at one specific moment rather than continuously over time.
poland other
Poland is a country in Europe.

Ponemon Institute is a research organization known for studies about privacy, data protection, and the cost of data breaches.
popular package concept
A popular package is a widely used software component that many projects download and depend on.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.

PowerShell scripts are files of Windows automation commands that can be used by administrators or abused by attackers.
Precise concept
Carefully targeted and intended to avoid unnecessary effects.
Preparation concept
Preparation is the incident-response phase where teams plan, train, and set up tools before an attack happens.
Previdian organization
Previdian is a named organization, product, or service referenced in security reporting.
Preview Update concept
An optional software update released for testing or early access before its normal wider release.
Prioritization concept
Prioritization means deciding which issues or tasks should be handled first based on importance or risk.
Prisma Access product
A cloud-based security product from Palo Alto Networks that protects users and remote access to applications.
Private information concept
Private information is personal or confidential data that should not be shared without permission.
private key concept
A private key is secret cryptographic data used to prove identity or decrypt information and must be kept confidential.
private sector organization
The private sector is the part of the economy made up of businesses and organizations not run by the government.

A privilege escalation flaw is a vulnerability that lets someone gain more access rights than they should have.
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privilege-escalation vulnerability vulnerability

privileged access concept
Privileged access is a higher level of permission that lets a user or system make important changes or view sensitive information.
privileged account concept
A privileged account is a user account with extra powers, such as changing settings, reading sensitive data, or managing other users.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.

A probe is an attempt to test a system for weaknesses or useful information before an attack.
process memory concept
Process memory is the part of a computer’s memory used by a running program.
Product Plans concept
Confidential or internal plans for developing, launching, or changing products.
production concept
Production is the live environment where real users and real data are handled.
production environment concept
A production environment is the live system that real users or customers depend on, unlike a test environment.
production systems concept
Production systems are the real live systems an organization uses to run its services or business.
Productivity Tool tool
Software designed to help people organize work, communicate, create documents, or complete tasks.

A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt injection technique

A technique where malicious input is crafted to manipulate an AI model into ignoring its instructions or revealing sensitive data.

prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.

Proofpoint is a cybersecurity company known for email security, threat intelligence, and data protection products.

Proofs of concept are small demonstrations showing that an idea, exploit, or vulnerability can work in practice.

Research owned or controlled by an organization and not meant for public release.
protected process concept
A Windows process given extra safeguards to prevent untrusted software from modifying or controlling it.
provenance attestations concept
Signed records that show where software was built and how it was published.

proxies tool

also: PTRACE_SEIZE, PTRACE_INTERRUPT, PTRACE_GETREGSET

Public disclosure is the act of making information, such as a security flaw, available to the public.

Public exploit code is attack code shared openly that shows how to take advantage of a vulnerability.
public exploits concept

The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
public services concept
Services provided by government to citizens, such as healthcare or transportation.

Publicly disclosed means information has been made available for the public to know.
pull request concept

push technique

pypi

QA concept
QA, short for quality assurance, is the process of testing software to find problems before it is released.

quarantined concept
Quarantined means a suspicious file, email, or system has been isolated so it cannot easily cause harm while it is investigated.

Requests sent to a database to retrieve, add, change, or remove information.

Extra name-and-value data added to a web address to tell a server how to handle a request.

ransomware attacks technique

RC4 is an older encryption method that was once widely used but is now considered unsafe for protecting sensitive data.

RCE, or remote code execution, is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands or programs on someone else's system from afar.
Readiness concept
Readiness is the state of being prepared to perform a task, job, or mission effectively.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
Reasoning concept
Reasoning is the process of working through information logically to reach an answer or decision.
Reasoning effort concept
Reasoning effort is a measure of how much computational work or depth an AI system uses to solve a task.
recommendation concept
A recommendation is suggested guidance or an action that someone should consider taking to reduce risk or solve a problem.
reconnaissance technique

Recorded Future organization
Recorded Future is one of the organizations named in the article.
Recover concept
Recover is a cybersecurity function focused on restoring systems, data, and services after an incident.
recovery phrase concept

The theft and transfer of a cryptocurrency wallet's secret recovery phrase to an attacker.
recovery phrases concept
Recovery phrases are lists of words used to restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet or other secured account.

Red Hat organization
Red Hat is a technology company known for enterprise Linux and related software.
redirect concept

redirect URI concept
A redirect URI is the web address an identity service sends a user back to after login or authorization.
also: redirect URIs, reply URL, real reply location, real destination
reflectiz

The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.

A vulnerability technique that uses directory paths such as ../ to access files outside an intended folder.
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
relays concept
Relays are systems that pass network traffic or messages from one place to another, such as email servers forwarding mail between senders and recipients.
release candidate concept
A nearly finished pre-release version of software that is being tested before a final release.
remediated concept
Remediated means a security issue has been fixed or otherwise addressed.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.

Remediation workflows are planned steps for fixing security issues after they are found.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.

Remote access tools let someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
remote attacker concept
A remote attacker is someone who tries to exploit a system over a network without needing physical access to it.

A remote code execution flaw is a serious bug that can let an attacker run commands on a system from somewhere else over a network.
remote command execution vulnerability
Remote command execution is when an attacker can run operating-system commands on another computer over a network.
remote control technique
Remote control means operating a computer, phone, or system from another location over a network.

A technology that lets you see and control a computer's desktop from another device over a network.
Remote desktop connections concept
Network connections that let someone view and control another computer from a distance.
remote desktop services tool

Remote Devices concept
Computers, phones, or other equipment that connect to an organization's systems from outside its main locations.
Remote IT Worker concept
A remote IT worker is a technology employee who performs their job away from the employer's office.
Remote workers concept
People who do their jobs away from the employer's usual office, often from home.
remote, unauthenticated attacker concept
A remote, unauthenticated attacker is someone who can attack over a network without first logging in.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
Reprompt tool
Reprompt is a named AI security tool, feature, or technique referenced in security reporting.
Reputation concept
A trust score or history used by security systems to judge whether a sender, website, or file is likely safe.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
Resecurity organization
Resecurity is a cybersecurity company that provides threat intelligence and security services.
Reseller Network concept
A reseller network is a group of businesses authorized or used to sell another company's products.
resellers organization
Resellers are companies or people that sell products or services made by another vendor.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Restart concept

Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
reverse shell technique
A reverse shell is a technique where a compromised computer connects back to an attacker and gives them a command-line session.

Reverse Shells technique
A remote command connection in which an infected computer calls back to an attacker's system for instructions.
RHEL product
Red Hat Enterprise Linux, a commercially supported Linux distribution widely used in corporate and government environments.
risk cohorts concept
Groups of similar vulnerabilities used to help organizations prioritize which risks to address first.
Risk Controls concept
Safeguards designed to identify, reduce, or stop harmful or suspicious activity.
RITA tool
A network-security analysis tool that helps investigators identify unusual activity and connections.
romance scams technique
Online fraud where criminals build fake romantic relationships to trick victims into sending money or sensitive information.
root concept
The superuser account on Unix and Linux systems that has unlimited control over the entire computer.
root access concept
Having complete administrative control over a computer or network, allowing unrestricted system changes.
root privileges concept
Root privileges are the highest level of control on Unix-like systems, allowing a user or program to change almost anything.
root-level concept
Root-level means having the highest level of control over a device or operating system.
root-level access concept
Root-level access is the highest level of control on many systems, allowing someone to change almost anything.
root-level control concept

In a mixture-of-experts AI model, a router chooses which specialized components should process each input.
routers product

rubygems

run code concept

run-at tool
run-at is a task or scheduling-style name referenced in security reporting.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russian-speaking concept
Russian-speaking describes people or groups that use Russian, often in reporting about cybercrime communities.
Russian-speaking victims concept
People who speak Russian and were targeted or harmed by a scam or other crime.

also: PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
safety measures concept
Safety measures are steps taken to reduce risk and protect people, accounts, data, or systems from harm.
sandbox-escape technique

A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
scam accounts concept
Scam accounts are online accounts created or used to trick people, steal money, or impersonate others.
Scam messages concept
Scam messages are texts, emails, or chats designed to trick people into sending money, data, or access.
scam websites concept
Scam websites are fake or deceptive sites created to steal money, passwords, or personal information.
scammers threat-actor
Scammers are people who trick others to steal money, information, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanner tool
A scanner is a tool that searches for information or problems automatically.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
Scanning tools tool
Scanning tools are programs that check systems or networks for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
scheduled-tasks

scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
screen-capture technique

screenshot concept
A screenshot is a captured image of what is shown on a screen.
screenshots concept
Images that capture what is currently shown on a computer screen.

A small removable memory card used to store files on devices such as cameras and recorders.

security checks technique
Security checks are tests or reviews used to find risks, weaknesses, or unsafe behavior in a system.
Security Companies organization
Security companies are businesses that provide cybersecurity products, research, consulting, or incident-response services.
security controls concept
Security controls are safeguards, such as settings, tools, or policies, used to reduce risk.

Security findings concept
Security findings are issues discovered during testing or review that may indicate weaknesses attackers could exploit.
also: findings
security gaps concept
